review.feedback: English draft resting on a synthetic fixture: an SIR model applied to a belief by analogy, with assumed reproduction numbers (4/5, 6/5, 3), one initial holder, 14 and 1,400 agents, 10,000 seeded runs per case checked against the exact jump-chain distribution (42 self-checks pass). Its observed part is a snapshot at Demerzel commit 4b03838800dcd4894f1e026461979bff1d985ca8 showing that the repository records no holder passing a belief on to another agent: of 21 belief files, the 12 with content have one evaluator and 9 are empty scaffolds; two cite a recommendation message that its schema describes as coming from ix's ML pipeline (the two messages are not in the repository), which makes them adoptions from a document; none of 722 JSON files under state/ has the shape of a belief snapshot or a knowledge state, or a key naming a teacher, a learner or a message's sender (origin_repo, origin_agent). No rate can be estimated, so the model is untested on the project. The research cycle refutes the first half of the expectation written in the module notes: two humps appear only at R0 = 3, and there the deterministic curve does describe the upper hump. Human subject review, learner trial, translation and publication remain pending.
